svg.title: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine: The installer refuses cleanly, sets up a bare machine through the pipe, and says what to do next
svg.text: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine
Scenario: The installer refuses cleanly, sets up a bare machine through the pipe, and says what to do next
Without curl, the installer refuses cleanly
The one-line install sets up the bare machine
Following that advice opens the merge request
With no terminal at all, nothing is asked

g.text: When the developer runs the installer on a fresh machine without curl,
it stops at its first check and says to install curl first
A brand-new Ubuntu machine, with the installer file copied onto it. One typed line: "type"
answers "not found" for curl, git and unzip, then the installer runs.
It prints its title and stops at its very first check: "curl is required but not installed."
It says to install curl and run it again, and exits with code 1 before changing anything.

text.tspan: type curl git unzip; bash /tmp/install.sh; echo "exit code: $?"

g.text: When the developer installs curl and pipes the installer from GitLab into bash, the
installer asks before installing Git
The same terminal, cleared. The developer installs curl with sudo, as told, then runs the one-line install from the
README: curl downloads the installer from GitLab and bash runs it straight from the pipe. The test GitLab serves it the
way gitlab.com does.
The installer says Git is required, at least version 2.34.0, and waits on "Install Git now? [Y/n]:". Bash is reading the
script from the pipe, so the installer reads the answer from the keyboard instead.

text.tspan: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y curl && curl -fsSL

g.text: And the installer asks before adding gum and glow, then asks what to
install, all through the pipe
The developer pressed Enter on each question, which means yes: Git, then task, then uv. This
card starts at the last plain question, "Install gum and glow?", plain because gum is the
tool that would make it pretty.
Once both are installed, the installer lists its two choices, "Complete framework" and
"Choose components", and asks "Install the complete DevSecOps framework?". Version numbers
show as v<version>, since they move with each release.
Then the setup finds unzip missing and installs it with sudo by itself
The developer keeps the complete framework and presses Enter on every Copier question. The
installer builds the project, then runs its setup, task devsecops:init, and the output
scrolls on for minutes.
This part scrolled by on the way: the setup says "unzip is required before task
devsecops:init.", installs it with sudo on its own, and ends on "unzip installed
successfully!". Apt's progress lines are left out.
And the installer stops and says the project needs a GitLab remote
The end of the run. The setup reaches "Configuring GitLab project..." and its GitLab sign-in check, glab:auth:ensure,
stops it: "No 'origin' remote configured. Add a GitLab remote, then re-run." The folder is not linked to any GitLab
project, so the framework has nowhere to go yet.
The developer then types echo "exit code: $?": the run ended with exit code 201, and the prompt is back.
Then once the developer links the folder to a GitLab project and runs the setup again,
GitLab shows the framework merge request into the main branch
In the same terminal, the developer turns the folder into a git repository, adds an empty GitLab project as its origin
remote and runs the setup again. The sign-in to GitLab with glab was done off screen.
GitLab's page for the merge request the setup opened: "chore: initialize devsecops framework", Open, from the
init-framework-devsecops branch into the main branch. The project's random name shows as "project". The merge box and
the tab counters are hidden, as they follow the pipelines GitLab starts on its own.

text.tspan: git init && git remote add origin https://gitlab.com/<namespace>/<project>.git && task devsecops:init

g.text: Then on a machine with no terminal at all, as in a CI job, the same installer asks nothing
and installs the complete framework
A new empty folder on the same machine, and one typed line that runs the installer the way a CI job does: setsid leaves
it no terminal, </dev/null leaves it nothing to read, and TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false skips the GitLab part, as the README
advises for a folder with no GitLab project.
Nobody answers anything and everything goes to /tmp/ci.log. The run ends with exit code 0, and the log ends on
"Installation complete!" and "Run 'task' to see available commands."

text.tspan: TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false setsid -w bash /tmp/install.sh </dev/null >/tmp/ci.log 2>&1; echo "exit code: $?"; tail

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 7 steps · 7 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
